title: Bell size and bore of the trombone
summary: They compare bell sizes and Henry says a big bore gives more volume on the street.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: That's a rather small bell, isn't it, compared to some smaller...
Well, the only bell larger than this is a symphony model bass trombone. This is a tenor trombone.
Yeah. I thought Albert Warner's bell on that con, because it looked a little bigger, was it? Maybe just...
It's about the same size. There's no difference in the bell. It's a nice bell.
No, you take a... They're making... The old people make a smaller bell. It's as large in here, but it's small here. See, they cut part of this rim off.
They almost have a smaller bell. They have a smaller bell than this. Never seen one. F.E.O.'s. Of course, it'd be a good trombone. Oh, yeah.
They're wonderful. But you take a trombone that has a big bore here, from here to here, you get more volume out of it for on the street.
In that last joint before the bell.
Yeah. Right in here. From there on up to the bell.
